stem: Which distinction does the position-control slide make between some stepper-equipped manipulators and most force/torque-driven manipulators?

options.text: For force/torque-driven manipulators, inverse kinematics alone supplies the required actuator effort
For force/torque-driven manipulators, computing nominal dynamics alone fully solves trajectory tracking
Some can execute a desired trajectory directly; most need an algorithm to compute the effort that causes the motion
Some stepper-equipped manipulators need torque commands, while most other manipulators directly accept trajectories without effort calculation

assumptions: Report the introductory course distinction; this is not a universal guarantee for all stepper-motor systems.

citations.locator: Lecture 1 physical PDF page 39; printed slide 39; main text and associated figure
citations.evidenceText:
Linear Position Control
•  Some manipulators are equipped with stepper motors or other actuators that
   can execute a desired trajectory directly
•  However, most of the manipulators are driven by actuators that supply a
   force/torque that will cause the desired motion.
•   In this case, an algorithm is needed to compute torques that will cause the
   desired motion.
•  The problem of dynamics is central to the design of such algorithms, but does
   not in itself constitute a solution.
•  A primary concern of the position control system is to
    –  automatically compensate for errors in knowledge of the
       parameters of the system
    –  and to suppress the disturbances that try to perturb the
       system from the desired trajectory.
